Subject: Redwood: intermittent long-tail latency and 500s — urgent

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a rise in end-to-end latency for inference calls yesterday afternoon. Most requests are fine, but ~1-2% are taking 8-22s and some return 500s. This is affecting our chat flows and an automated job that retries aggressively.

Example request IDs (from our side):
- req_20261114_aa21
- req_20261114_bb87
- req_20261114_cc03

I attached a CSV with our request ids and a small sample of timestamps. From our traces it looks like requests are getting stuck in a queued state before reaching the model. Can you confirm if there were infra changes or throttles applied to our Dedicated pool?

We need an ETA on a fix and whether you expect any customer credits. CCing our platform team.

Thanks,
Sara White

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

On Mon, Nov 14, 2026 at 9:27 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Sara — apologies for the disruption. I'm escalating to engineering and SRE right away and will own coordination.

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed matching p99/p999 tail increases in the ACME dedicated pool starting ~2026-11-14T15:05:00Z (their timestamps roughly align with Sara's CSV).
- Root cause signal: queueing backlog at the gateway layer—requests queueing while waiting for available worker contexts. We see backpressure events where the pool's concurrency cap for the active model variant is saturated for short bursts.
- Contributing factor: Two worker nodes in the pool were rebooted due to a kernel patch; autoscaler rebalanced and regained capacity, but during the rebalance we hit a transient capacity shortfall. This produced longer queue times and occasional timeouts/500s.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:35 PT):
1) Increased concurrency cap for ACME's pool from 250 -> 300 for the affected model variant (temporary).
2) Enabled short-term prioritization for interactive chat routes for the next 60 minutes.
3) Kicked off a targeted node health sweep and held off non-critical maintenance for their pool.

Initial result: tail latency reduced but not yet to normal baseline — p999 still elevated for a small set of requests. We're collecting span traces and will replay failing request ids in a controlled window.

Next actions for Monday (requested by Lauren):
- Prepare a concise one-page exec brief describing timeline, root cause, immediate mitigation, longer-term fix (autoscaler pre-warm + stronger soft-eviction policies), and a recommended customer credit.
- Schedule a 30-min bridge with ACME and our execs — propose Mon 10:00 AM PT.

Attachments: datadog-spans-acme-20261114.png, perf-trace-20261114.txt

Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Additional SRE notes + logs (snippet):

[2026-11-14T15:06:12Z] pool=acme-dedicated-12 event=backpressure reason="worker_eviction" queued=342 active=248 cap=250
[2026-11-14T15:06:13Z] pool=acme-dedicated-12 action=reject status=503 req=req_20261114_bb87
[2026-11-14T15:06:30Z] autoscaler=rebalance nodes_removed=2 nodes_added=2

Mitigation suggestion (safe short term):
- Keep increased concurrency cap (300) for 3 hours and monitor. We should also enable a short TTL on queued requests so extreme tails fail fast (reduces customer retries).
- For the next week, add a pre-warm policy: if node replacement is planned in a pool with >200 active concurrency, pre-spin one node before eviction.

Cost note: transient increased compute spend for ACME's pool while cap is higher; recommend we estimate impact and propose a partial credit if they incur >5% excess spend relative to baseline during the incident window.

--
Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead
